name: D.O.A.
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Joe Keithley, who calls himself Joey Shithead, put "hardcore" on an album in 1981, kept touring it for four decades and in 2018 won a seat on Burnaby city council.

eras.title: Home from Toronto with a new name
eras.text: Joe Keithley came back from a failed Toronto trip with a new name and a band that started as a joke about Ramones records. Within months D.O.A. had a single, a San Francisco fan in Jello Biafra and a reputation for volume.

years.src: The Skulls (Canadian band) - Wikipedia · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories · Vancouver Magazine: Joey Shithead: Forever Punk
years.h: The Skulls collapse in Toronto and Joe Keithley starts D.O.A. at home
years.p: The Burnaby band had gone from rock to punk after seeing the Ramones, and it left no records behind.
years.xp:
The Skulls were Keithley, bassist Brian Goble, guitarist Simon Werner and drummer Ken Montgomery, all veterans of the rock band Stone Crazy. Wikipedia says they left Vancouver because the club circuit was mostly hostile and the only other punk bands were the Furies and the Dishrags.

Montgomery, known as Dimwit, is the one who told Keithley to call himself Shithead, Keithley says, and the first name floated for the band was Joey Shithead And The Marching Morons. On the band name he told Punknews: "We always said the most famous D.O.A. was JFK."

Vancouver Magazine reports that an earlier Keithley band's first paid gig, at the Grasslands Motor Inn in Merritt on June 5, 1977, ended with the manager firing them despite a signed contract for $500 over four nights.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories
years.h: A singer with no sense of rhythm fronts the first show at the Japanese Hall
years.p: Harry Homo sang for Keithley, drummer Chuck Biscuits and bassist Randy Rampage, and was dismissed soon after. Keithley has held the mic ever since.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says a guitarist called Randy Romance lasted through March 1978, and Brad Kent joined in June and was dismissed in September. Keithley has been the lead vocalist ever since, and the only constant member.

Over the decades the band has counted five bassists and roughly eight drummers, Keithley told the Dallas Observer.

years.src: Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Disco Sucks: 500 copies, paid for with unemployment cheques
years.p: D.O.A. recorded and mixed the self-released EP in one eight-hour session. Wikipedia says it topped the chart at San Francisco's KUSF.
years.xp:
Keithley told Punknews how the money arrived: "My girlfriend at the time had some unemployment checks and I said 'how about a fine investment in the band?'" The lyrics were still being finished during the session.

They mailed copies to record shops in California, New York, Chicago and Toronto, plus college radio stations.

years.cap: Randy Rampage and Joey Shithead at Rock Against Racism, Lincoln Park, Chicago
years.src: Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Something Better Change - Wikipedia
yt: Keithley on the first San Francisco trip and the Mabuhay incident
years.h: Mabuhay Gardens throws Keithley out, and Jello Biafra stops the show
years.p: Keithley shook up a beer and sprayed the stage manager. Four security guards removed him, and Biafra refused to play until he was let back in.
years.xp:
Punknews has Keithley sneaking beers in and drinking one at the front of the stage. Dirk Dirksen, who ran the club, banned him for life. Keithley remembers Biafra's words as: "Stop the show, we aren't playing unless you let Joey Shithead back in here!"

Wikipedia dates D.O.A.'s first San Francisco shows to August 1978, at the Mabuhay. Biafra's Alternative Tentacles later issued the compilation Bloodied But Unbowed, reissued Something Better Change in 2002, and put out Last Scream of the Missing Neighbors with Biafra singing for D.O.A.

eras.title: Opening for the Clash
eras.text: D.O.A. made a first North American tour, hired a manager, added a second guitarist and survived one bad night at UBC. By 1980 the lineup was back together, with the songs for a debut album.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · MONTECRISTO: That Time the Clash Played Soccer With a Bunch of Vancouver Punks
years.h: D.O.A. gets the opening slot for the Clash at the Pacific Coliseum
years.p: The Clash's October 1979 Vancouver date put D.O.A. on a bill with a band they had grown up listening to. The two had already met, on a soccer pitch.
years.xp:
Earlier that year, on January 31, 1979, the Clash played the Commodore and, before the show, took on local punks at soccer in a Vancouver park. Nick Jones of the Pointed Sticks told Montecristo: "They beat us... We lost 5-3." The players named include members of the Pointed Sticks, the Rabid, Corsage and the Subhumans.

D.O.A. had toured North America for the first time in May 1979, and afterward hired Vancouver journalist and activist Ken Lester as manager. Wikipedia says Dave Gregg joined as second guitarist late that year, and that a disastrous UBC Student Union Building show led Biscuits and Rampage to quit, replaced briefly by Andy Graffiti and Simon "Stubby Pecker" Wilde. Keithley took them both back in March 1980.

years.src: Something Better Change - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Three years of songs go onto Something Better Change
years.p: Producer Richard Drake recorded it in Vancouver between 1977 and 1980, and it came out on Friends Records. Wikipedia notes it was out of print for nearly two decades.
years.xp:
Trouser Press describes the record as tighter than the band's earlier singles, with two-guitar arrangements. Sudden Death reissued it in 2000, Alternative Tentacles in 2002 with a re-recorded "Disco Sucks" added, and it came out again in 2011.

Critic Jack Rabid called the first two albums "revolutionary" and distinct from each other, and Ballast magazine ranked Something Better Change number 10 among its top 50 Canadian albums in 2013.

eras.title: The name goes on the cover
eras.text: A San Francisco magazine had been trying out the word hardcore. D.O.A. put it on a festival poster, then on an album, and within a year the rhythm section that made the record was gone.

years.cap: Chuck Biscuits, Randy Rampage, Dave Gregg and Joe Keithley at Hardcore 81, Vancouver, Feb 14, 1981
years.big: "We were the progenitors of spreading that name around"
q: We were the progenitors of spreading that name around
years.src: Alternative Press: DOA discuss the legacy of second album 'Hardcore 81' · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A)
years.h: Black Flag drives to Vancouver for the two-night Hardcore 81 festival
years.p: Section 8 filled in for 7 Seconds, who couldn't make it. Keithley named the album he was about to make after the festival.
years.xp:
Keithley told Punknews that a San Francisco magazine article in late 1980 had used "hardcore" for bands including D.O.A., Black Flag and the Circle Jerks. When D.O.A. organised the festival in Vancouver, he took the word for the record.

Alternative Press dates the festival to February and March 1981; Punknews says March.

years.src: Alternative Press: DOA discuss the legacy of second album 'Hardcore 81' · Hardcore '81 - Wikipedia
years.h: Eighteen minutes later, Hardcore '81 has named a genre
years.p: Released April 22, 1981, it is credited with popularizing the word for the whole genre. Wikipedia lists Sudden Death as the label.
years.xp:
Producer Tracy Marks got a first side of eleven minutes and a second of seven, per Alternative Press. The songs were written alongside the debut's, and the record includes a Led Zeppelin cover, "Communication Breakdown", with Keithley singing an octave below Robert Plant under an underwater vocal effect.

On relistening after a remaster that fixed tape dropouts, Keithley said: "Fuck, this is a really good record!" In 2019 it won the public vote for the Polaris Heritage Prize.

years.src: Randy Rampage - Wikipedia · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Chuck Biscuits - Wikipedia
years.h: Rampage gets fired after New Year's, and Biscuits leaves after a California tour
years.p: Brian Goble joined as "Wimpy Roy", on bass and second voice, and Dimwit, the old Skulls drummer, went back behind the kit.
years.xp:
Keithley dismissed bassist Randy Rampage after the New Year's Eve show. Dimwit moved to bass for a spell, then back to the kit when Goble arrived.

Wikipedia says Chuck Biscuits left to join Black Flag; his own page says he played with them only briefly in 1982, after which conflict with Henry Rollins pushed him toward the Circle Jerks. He later joined Danzig in 1987 on Rick Rubin's invitation and left in 1994 over royalty disputes. Rampage returned to D.O.A. for the 2002 album Win the Battle.

years.src: War on 45 - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A. · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories
yt: Early-80s documentary: touring western Canada and making the "War" video
years.h: A Dylan cover, a Temptations cover and a reggae song make War on 45
years.p: An eight-song 12-inch on Alternative Tentacles and Sudden Death. Robert Christgau gave it an A-.
years.xp: The covers are Bob Dylan's "Masters of War" and the Temptations' "War". Trouser Press likened the band's sound to a keyboardless Stranglers. Keithley told the Dallas Observer: "It has some straight up punk rock and a reggae song. I think the variety made it fun for everybody."

eras.title: Lawyers, hard rock and Biafra
eras.text: D.O.A. toured harder than most, reached Europe, tried on hard rock and fought a label over who owned its records. The decade closed with a record fronted by Jello Biafra and a farewell show.

years.src: Squamish Five - Wikipedia · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Let's Wreck the Party - Wikipedia · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A)
years.h: Burn It Down: a single for the Vancouver Five's defence fund
years.p: Subhumans bassist Gerry Hannah was one of five anarchists arrested in January 1983. D.O.A. put out a single to pay for the defence.
years.xp:
The Squamish Five bombed a BC Hydro substation on Vancouver Island in May 1982 and moved 550 kg of dynamite toward Toronto's Litton Industries plant that October; the RCMP arrested them on January 20, 1983.

Keithley told Punknews he backed the defence but not the bombings: blowing things up wasn't the way, he said. In a 1984 interview he said the single raised at least $2,500 and that he was a character witness at Hannah's sentencing, per Wikipedia. The song "Trial by Media" on Let's Wreck the Party is about Hannah.

years.cap: Dave Gregg at the Smilin' Buddha, Vancouver
years.src: Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A)
years.h: Bloodied But Unbowed gets D.O.A. ready for Europe
years.p: Alternative Tentacles compiled the first two albums and the singles for a UK and European run, per Punknews.
years.xp: Keithley says he founded Sudden Death Records to keep control: "I thought this way I could put out what records I wanted whenever I wanted." The label released D.O.A. and also the Pointed Sticks and the Young Canadians.

years.src: Let's Wreck the Party - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A. · The Canadian Encyclopedia: D.O.A. · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · The Big Takeover: You're D.O.A.! An Interview With Joey Keithley
years.h: D.O.A. goes hard rock on purpose with Let's Wreck the Party
years.p: Alternative Tentacles put it out to get ahead of a demo tape another label had obtained. It includes a cover of "Singin' in the Rain".
years.xp:
Producer Brian MacLeod helped the band lean into hard rock; the band felt hardcore had lost political relevance. "General Strike" had first appeared on the John Peel session EP, for striking British miners. Trouser Press called the record "a cutting and witty record".

That year the Canadian Encyclopedia counts D.O.A. playing 105 cities in over a dozen countries. Keithley told Punknews of a Leeds show where the PA lay on its side because the venue feared punks would knock it over. Staff locked up without turning off the beer taps, so the band helped themselves.

Keithley told The Big Takeover that a mid-1980s legal fight with a label cost $50,000 US, about $77,000 Canadian at the time.

years.src: Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · The Big Takeover: You're D.O.A.! An Interview With Joey Keithley
years.h: A trumpet turns up on True (North) Strong and Free
years.p: Trouser Press hears Canadian identity and anti-fascist politics, and more instruments than D.O.A. had used before.
years.xp:
Drummer Kerr Belliveau lasted three weeks in 1986, recorded the Expo Hurts Everyone 7-inch and part of this record, and was replaced by Jon Card of Winnipeg's Personality Crisis, who stayed through 1990. Card died April 8, 2024, at 63; no cause was given publicly.

Keithley told The Big Takeover that he has recovered most of the band's early albums from labels, but that this one and Murder were still unavailable.

years.cap: Playbill for a D.O.A. show, July 22, 1988
years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: D.O.A. fires manager Ken Lester, and guitarist Dave Gregg leaves
years.p: Lester had managed the band since 1979. Chris Prohom of the Dayglo Abortions took Gregg's place.

years.src: Last Scream of the Missing Neighbors - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A.
years.h: Jello Biafra sings for D.O.A. on Last Scream of the Missing Neighbors
years.p: Six songs on Alternative Tentacles, produced by Biafra and Cecil English, including the 14-minute "Full Metal Jackoff".
years.xp:
Biafra sings; Keithley, Prohom, Brian Goble and Jon Card play. Trouser Press praised Biafra's "whiny" vocals against the band's "meat-and-cojones guitar power", and said it carries on the Dead Kennedys' work. It ends with a cover of "We Gotta Get Out of This Place".

"That's Progress" appeared on the Rock Against Bush, Vol. 1 compilation.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A.
years.h: Keithley calls it quits with a last show at the Commodore
years.p: He announced the breakup in August 1990, and promoter Dirk Dirksen suggested a West Coast farewell tour that ended in Vancouver.
years.xp:
The band's last album before the break was Murder in 1990, with a rawer sound that Wikipedia calls almost thrash metal. The live album Talk Minus Action Equals Zero came out afterward, while Keithley pursued acting.

Trouser Press describes the live album as the farewell record. D.O.A. stayed dormant for about 19 months.

eras.title: A three-piece with something to say
eras.text: D.O.A. came back with fewer people and a tougher outlook, then started losing friends. The record it made in the middle of that is one of the strongest of its career.

years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Keithley, Wimpy Roy and Ken Jensen put D.O.A. back together
years.p: Keithley told Exclaim! that was what he thought no new band was doing. The trio signed to Alternative Tentacles.
years.xp:
Exclaim! says Keithley had spent several months moving office furniture before the reunion. His reason: "I felt there hadn't been a new band coming along who was doing what we were doing." Jensen, from the band Red Tide, was recommended by NoMeansNo's John Wright, who also produced the records and played keyboards.

Keithley said he wanted to combine "the obnoxious loud qualities with humour and social activism."

years.src: Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive
years.h: John Wright of NoMeansNo produces 13 Flavours of Doom
years.p: Trouser Press credits his production with bringing back "spunk and inspiration".
years.xp: Alternative Tentacles also put out the compilation Dawning of a New Error that year, per Exclaim!.

years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Dimwit, who told Keithley to call himself Shithead, dies
years.p: Ken Montgomery died in the fall of 1994 of a heroin overdose, per Exclaim!. Keyboardist Ford Pier also joined on guitar that year.
years.xp: Keithley told Exclaim!: "He was not a junkie, I want to make that clear. He was an occasional user."

years.src: Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive
years.h: The Black Spot comes out after Ken Jensen dies in a house fire
years.p: John Wright drummed on the album. Alternative Tentacles put out a Ken Jensen memorial single with Red Tide.
years.xp: Trouser Press called it the band's tautest, most precise and hard-edged work, recorded amid the tragedy. Exclaim! says Brian O'Brien followed Wright as drummer.

years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · Brian Roy Goble - Wikipedia · Joe Keithley - Wikipedia · Exclaim!: R.I.P. Brian "Wimpy Roy" Goble of the Subhumans/D.O.A.
years.h: Wimpy Roy leaves after 14 years, and Keithley picks up the bass
years.p: Brian Goble quit after the Black Spot tour. Exclaim! says he was frustrated with label issues.
years.xp:
Keithley played bass himself from 1996 to 1998, per Wikipedia. That same year he ran for the BC Green Party in a provincial election, as he did again in 2001, when he had the second-highest vote share among the party's candidates after leader Adriane Carr.

Goble later rejoined the Subhumans, and died of a heart attack on December 7, 2014, aged 57. Keithley called him "a humanist, a great father, an incredible singer and bass player."

eras.title: A Metallica producer and a farewell tour
eras.text: A new drummer, an old bassist and the man who produced Metallica. Then Keithley went looking for a political job, and the band called it a day for a while.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · Vancouver Magazine: Joey Shithead: Forever Punk
years.h: Randy Rampage returns after twenty years for Win the Battle
years.p: Rampage played bass, then left again after the recording; Dan Yaremko took over.
years.xp:
Exclaim! says Rampage rejoined for European and Japanese tours before going back to longshoring work.

Wikipedia says Vancouver's mayor, Larry Campbell, declared December 21 D.O.A. Day for the band's 25th anniversary, in 2003. Vancouver Magazine gives the year as 2002.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Metallica's producer Bob Rock makes Northern Avenger
years.p: Randy Rampage played on the record and left before the tour. Dan Yaremko was back on bass for the 30th anniversary run.
years.xp: The 30th anniversary tour began in September 2008. Drummer the Great Baldini had left; James Hayden quit before recording and Floor Tom Jones took over.

years.cap: Joe Keithley playing with D.O.A., Montreal
years.src: The Globe and Mail: What happens when an old punk rocker enters politics · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Two thousand doors later, Keithley loses the NDP nomination by five votes
years.p: He was after the New Democratic Party nomination in Coquitlam-Burke Mountain, and D.O.A. went on hiatus while he campaigned.
years.xp:
The Globe and Mail reported that Keithley, then 56, knocked on about 2,000 doors over two months. He told the paper: "I've been a student of politics since I was 14, 15, 16." The five-vote margin comes from the Dallas Observer.

D.O.A.'s farewell tour started January 18, 2013, at Vancouver's Rickshaw Theatre, with dates in BC, Alberta and California.

eras.title: Same name, new rhythm section
eras.text: The farewell lasted about twenty months. A new drummer and bassist arrived, a song about a presidential candidate followed, and Keithley finally won an election.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: D.O.A. cancels its farewell and re-forms with Paddy Duddy and Mike Hodsall
years.p: Keithley posted the news on the Sudden Death Records site. An October Canadian tour supported the live album Welcome to Chinatown.
years.xp: Dave Gregg, the guitarist from 1979 to 1988, also died in 2014, Wikipedia says.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: D.O.A. takes on Donald Trump with "Fucked Up Donald"
years.p: The single came out in April 2016, aimed at Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump.

years.src: Invisible Oranges: D.O.A. Still Prepared To "Fight Back" After Four Decades
years.h: The 17th studio album, Fight Back, goes after inequality
years.p: Invisible Oranges caught up with Keithley four decades in, and he named inequality as the record's central theme.

years.src: Randy Rampage - Wikipedia
years.h: Randy Rampage, D.O.A.'s first bassist, dies at 58
years.p: Wikipedia cites reports that he died at his Vancouver home of an apparent heart attack. He played on the first two albums and returned twice.

years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A.'s Joe Keithley Elected to Burnaby City Council · Joe Keithley - Wikipedia
years.h: Keithley wins the last seat on Burnaby city council by 215 votes
years.p: As a Green, he broke the Burnaby Citizens Association's hold on the council, per Exclaim!.
years.xp: Keithley won the eighth and final seat with 15,745 votes. He had run as a Green in 2013, 2015 and 2017, taking 13.77% in the 2017 Burnaby-Lougheed provincial race, per Wikipedia. He was re-elected in 2022, and on December 15, 2025, Wikipedia says, he switched to the Burnaby Citizens Association.
